userJob: Pick the two type roles a page needs before writing any CSS
problem: The type is chosen last from whatever the framework installed, so the page inherits a neutral interface face and the design has no voice at any size
worksWhen: Every build, at plan time, before the first component
avoidWhen: The client's brand names its faces, where the brand outranks this entirely
mechanism: Typography: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Arial and Inter; opt instead for distinctive choices that elevate the frontend's aesthetics; unexpected, characterful font choices. Pair a distinctive display font with a refined body font.
risks: A display face with character used at every size, which turns character into noise
Choosing a face for its specimen rather than for the copy it has to set
mobileRules: The display face has its own scale step at 375px; the desktop size divided by a ratio usually overflows or clips
accessibilityRules: Body text at 4.5:1 and large display text at 3:1 against its actual ground
Check the face has the figures, diacritics and language coverage the copy needs before committing
genericnessNote: The instruction to avoid the default face is only half of it; without a subject-derived reason, builders converge on the same two or three alternatives.

userJob: Decide how many type roles the page needs and where the character goes
problem: One face is used for everything, so hierarchy has to be carried by size alone and the page grows a stack of near-identical sizes
worksWhen: Every build; two roles is the floor, not the target
avoidWhen: A brief that names a single-face system, where the constraint is the design
mechanism: At least two roles: a display face with real character used with restraint, and a body face that supports it. Not the pairing you would reach for on any other project. State the scale and the weights in the plan before any code, so a later size is chosen from the scale rather than invented at the component.
risks: Adding a third face for one label, which is a decision nobody made
A scale with eight steps, where four of them differ by two pixels and carry no meaning
mobileRules: Declare the mobile scale explicitly rather than inheriting the desktop ratio
Line length stays inside 35 to 60 characters at 375px
accessibilityRules: Line height 1.5 or more for body text
Weight and colour carry hierarchy alongside size, so a reader who has scaled text up still sees the levels
genericnessNote: Two roles is structural, but the pairing is where sameness enters, which is why the plan has to say why this pairing and not the usual one.

userJob: Decide whether a serif display face is justified on this brief
problem: Creative, premium and editorial briefs get a serif by reflex, so every craft brand ends up in one of two display serifs and the brand becomes invisible
worksWhen: The brand brief names a serif, or the family is genuinely editorial, luxury, publication, manuscript, heritage or vintage and you can say why this serif fits this brand
avoidWhen: Creative agency, design studio, modern brand, premium consumer, portfolio and lifestyle briefs, where the reflex is strongest and least earned
mechanism: "It feels creative / premium / editorial" is NOT a reason to reach for serif.
risks: Justifying the serif after choosing it, which is the reflex wearing an argument
Rotating to a different serif from the same two or three, which is the same default under another name
mobileRules: High-contrast serifs lose their thin strokes at small sizes and on low-density screens; check the body size actually used at 375px
accessibilityRules: Thin strokes reduce effective contrast, so measure the rendered result rather than the nominal colour value
genericnessNote: The serif reflex is one of the most tested defaults, and naming two banned faces only moves the convergence to the third.

userJob: Avoid the two display serifs that mark a page as machine chosen
problem: When a serif is justified, the same two faces are chosen, so the justification is real and the outcome is still the default
worksWhen: A serif has already been justified and the specific face is being picked
avoidWhen: The brand explicitly names one of them, where the brand wins
mechanism: Specifically BANNED as defaults: Fraunces and Instrument_Serif (the two LLM-favorite display serifs).
risks: Treating the named pair as the whole problem, when the mechanism is availability rather than those two files
Reusing the same replacement serif across consecutive projects, which recreates the pattern
mobileRules: Whatever face replaces them needs its own mobile scale step checked at 375px
accessibilityRules: Verify the replacement face carries the weights the scale assumes; a missing weight is synthesised and loses contrast
genericnessNote: Excluding two files is a narrow constraint, and the post is only useful together with the reason a serif was chosen at all.

userJob: Set an italic word inside a display headline without clipping it
problem: Display headlines are set with tight leading, and an italic word containing a descender is clipped by the line box, which looks like a rendering bug rather than a choice
worksWhen: Any display headline that emphasises a word in italic
avoidWhen: Body copy, where default leading already clears descenders
mechanism: When italic is used in display type and the word contains a descender letter (y g j p q), leading-[1] or leading-none will clip the descender.
risks: Fixing it by raising leading globally, which changes the whole headline rhythm to solve one word
Checking only the desktop render, where the clip may fall outside the visible line
mobileRules: Re-check every italic display word at 375px, where the wrap point changes which word sits on which line
accessibilityRules: Emphasis by italic is visual only; if the emphasis carries meaning, mark it up as emphasis rather than styling it
genericnessNote: A clearance rule is a rendering fix with no stylistic content.

userJob: Emphasise a word inside a headline without switching typeface
problem: A single word is set in a contrasting family to add interest, so the headline reads as two headlines spliced together
worksWhen: Any headline where one word carries the turn of the sentence
avoidWhen: A deliberate two-voice system where the second family is a documented role, not an accent
mechanism: When you want to emphasize a word within a headline, use italic or bold of the SAME font. Do NOT inject a random serif word into a sans headline, or the reverse, just to add visual interest.
risks: Replacing family-mixing with colour-mixing, which is the same move in another axis
Emphasising more than one word, which cancels the emphasis
mobileRules: Check the emphasised word does not land alone on its own line at 375px
accessibilityRules: If the emphasis changes meaning, use a semantic emphasis element rather than a styled span
genericnessNote: Keeping emphasis inside one family is a discipline, and which family is still the design's own choice.

userJob: Set body copy so a paragraph can be read without losing the line
problem: A body column inherits the container width, so paragraphs run the full page and the eye loses its place on the return sweep
worksWhen: Any running prose: editorial, about pages, documentation, long product descriptions
avoidWhen: Short interface strings and labels, where measure is not the constraint
mechanism: Cap the measure and set the leading together: roughly 60 to 75 characters per line on desktop, 35 to 60 at mobile widths, with line height between 1.5 and 1.75 for body text. Set the cap on the text element rather than on the section, so a wide section can still hold a narrow column.
risks: Capping the section instead of the paragraph, which also narrows figures and tables that needed the width
Raising line height on headings, where the same value opens gaps the composition did not intend
mobileRules: 16px minimum body size so the browser does not zoom on input focus
accessibilityRules: Text scales to 200 percent without loss of content, which a fixed-pixel column often breaks
Line height stays proportional when text is scaled, rather than being pinned in pixels
genericnessNote: A measure range constrains column width and leaves face, scale, colour and rhythm free.

userJob: Keep the number of distinct type sizes on the page under control
problem: Each component picks a size that looked right in isolation, so the page ends up with eleven sizes, four of which differ by a pixel and mean nothing
worksWhen: Any build with more than a handful of components
avoidWhen: A single-purpose page with one heading and one paragraph, where a scale is bureaucracy
mechanism: Write the scale and the weights into the plan before any code, and take every size in the code from that list. Changing your mind mid build means changing the plan first. A size that is not on the scale is a decision nobody recorded.
risks: A scale so fine that adjacent steps are indistinguishable, which is the same problem written down
Treating the scale as a house style carried between projects, which is how two clients get one page
mobileRules: Declare the mobile steps as their own list rather than as a ratio applied to the desktop list
accessibilityRules: Sizes expressed in relative units so a reader's own text scaling still works
Hierarchy readable when every size is scaled up together, which means weight and space carry some of it
genericnessNote: A declared scale prevents drift but is easy to copy between projects, so the scale itself has to come from the subject's material.

userJob: Write the words with the same intent as the spacing
problem: Copy is written last and least, so the design reverts to template at exactly the layer a reader actually reads
worksWhen: Every build, before the layout is defended
avoidWhen: Never; a page whose text is a placeholder is not finished, whatever it looks like
mechanism: Name things by what the reader controls and recognises, never by how the system is built. Say what a thing does rather than selling it. Active voice by default, and a control keeps the same word all the way through, so a button that says Publish produces a message that says Published. Errors say what happened and what to do, in the interface's voice, and never apologise. An empty state is an invitation rather than an apology.
risks: Cute copy that reads as thoughtful and does not track, which is worse than plain copy
Two labels for one intent across nav, hero and footer, which splits the reader's model
mobileRules: Long labels wrap at 375px; shorten the label rather than shrinking the control
accessibilityRules: The visible label and the accessible name match, so voice control users can say what they see
Error text is announced as well as displayed
genericnessNote: Copy written from the reader's own vocabulary is the least transferable material on the page.
